nodes.title: Geometric Be chart and degree
nodes.statement: For algebraically closed F and nonzero t in P_1, the imported chart D_+(t) is Spec(Be), where Be=(B[1/t])^{phi=1}=(P[1/t])_0. This identifies its closed points with the orbits outside div(t), and its completed local rings with B_dR,y^plus. The function nu(f)=-ord_infinity(f), f nonzero in Be, is a nonnegative integer, additive on products, and vanishes exactly on E^times. Be is Bezout, and the resulting minimum-degree argument proves it is a PID. The curve, its Picard group and geometric HN theory remain imported from VB2. For the geometric chart the source also supplies weak almost-Euclidean division: for a,b in Be, b nonzero, there are q,r with a=bq+r and either r=0 or nu(r)<=nu(b). This weak inequality alone is not used as a Euclidean-domain criterion.
hypotheses: Standing E, F and norm conventions of the reader document; extra restrictions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Identify the section-localization chart of the parent Proj and compare its vanishing ideals using the orbit-divisor map.
Use the weighted degree-zero formula for a principal divisor to see nu>=0 and nu=0 precisely for a unit.

For a nonzero ideal choose an element of minimum nu. For any other element use a Bezout gcd; its degree cannot be smaller, so the gcd is associated to the chosen element and that element divides every ideal member.

For weak almost-Euclidean division, divide homogeneous representatives and use surjectivity of evaluation of the required positive-degree section on the finite zero divisor of b. A correction with only the pole at infinity leaves remainder pole order at most nu(b); retain the non-strict inequality.
acceptance: Be means invariant functions after inverting t; it is not Frac(B)^{phi=1}. The generic degree argument is one milestone statable over the pinned ring API.

sources.match: Be means invariant functions after inverting t; it is not Frac(B)^{phi=1}. The generic degree argument is one milestone statable over the pinned ring API.

nodes.title: Continuous descent of de Rham jets
nodes.statement: Let C be the completed algebraic closure of F and z a finite-orbit point above y with stabilizer G_L, identified by tilting with the absolute Galois group of K_y. The invariant ring (B_dR,z^plus)^{G_L} is B_dR,y^plus, and likewise for its finite jets. A finite-length B_dR,z^plus-module with continuous semilinear action has H^1_cont=0. Scalar extension gives an equivalence from finitely generated B_dR,y^plus-modules to finitely generated B_dR,z^plus-modules with semilinear G_L-action continuous on every finite jet; the inverse is fixed vectors. No higher-cohomology assertion is included. The perfectoid Tate–Sen estimates needed for effectivity are request R-TATE.
hypotheses: Standing E, F and norm conventions of the reader document; extra restrictions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: For n=1 use the marked-untilt field correspondence and the almost trace estimates after tilting.
Obtain quantitative cochain corrections for the finite-dimensional semilinear residue modules, not just the scalar invariant-field equality.

Induct through the finite filtration using its residue-field graded pieces, control continuity of the lifts, and identify the completed local comparison. Do not substitute the fully faithful statement of P9 for this effectivity step.

For a finitely generated module, descend its torsion and free pieces through all finite jets, prove compatibility of the descended presentations, and pass to the complete inverse limit with norm-controlled lifts. This extra inverse-limit effectivity is included in R-TATE.
acceptance: The scalar fixed-field result alone does not imply descent of all continuous semilinear modules. This target carries a recorded supplier gap.

sources.locator: Proposition 7.1.1 and preceding topology conventions, p. 262
sources.match: The scalar fixed-field result alone does not imply descent of all continuous semilinear modules. This target carries a recorded supplier gap.

nodes.title: Galois cohomology of positive eigenvectors
nodes.statement: For d>=1 and a finite-dimensional continuous E-representation V of G_F, H^1_cont(G_F,P_(C,d) tensor_E V)=0. If V is nonzero, its H^0 is nonzero. Both statements are compatible with the Banach topologies and finite scalar extension. The assertion of a nonzero H^0 explicitly excludes V=0.
hypotheses: Standing E, F and norm conventions of the reader document; extra restrictions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Choose a G_F-stable O_E-lattice in V and use the small-ball filtration of the Lubin–Tate parametrization for d=1.
Identify the successive quotients with m_C,rho tensor the residue lattice, and apply quantitative almost trace cohomology. Correct the cochains with shrinking errors and use completeness.
Deduce d>1 through the fundamental exact sequences and jet descent; prove nonzero invariants by lifting a nonzero invariant in the first nonzero small quotient.
acceptance: Continuous cohomology uses the Banach module topology. The arbitrary perfectoid-untilt estimates remain explicit in R-TATE.

sources.match: Continuous cohomology uses the Banach module topology. The arbitrary perfectoid-untilt estimates remain explicit in R-TATE.

nodes.title: Dedekind Be over a perfect field
nodes.statement: For any perfect F and nonzero t in P_(F,1), Be_F=(B_F[1/t])^{phi=1} is a Dedekind domain with units E^times. Its maximal ideals correspond to classical Frobenius orbits outside div(t). If f is nonzero then Be_F/(f) is the finite product, over the zeros of f off t, of B_dR,y^plus/Fil^(ord_y f); in particular each completed maximal localization is B_dR,y^plus.
hypotheses: Standing E, F and norm conventions of the reader document; extra restrictions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Over C the chart is a PID. Descend its quotient by f using H^1-vanishing of the filtered union t^(-k)P_(C,k).
Group geometric zeros into induced Galois modules using finite-orbit cosets and apply jet descent to each factor.

Use the resulting finite-product DVR-quotient characterization of a Dedekind domain, then recover maximal ideals and completions from these quotients. The no-zero eigenvector calculation gives units E^times.
acceptance: Dedekind replaces PID over general F; the quotient factors include higher jets and primitive-degree residue extensions.

sources.match: Dedekind replaces PID over general F; the quotient factors include higher jets and primitive-degree residue extensions.

nodes.title: Ideal classes and continuous characters
nodes.statement: For the general-field chart Be_F, Cl(Be_F) is canonically isomorphic to Hom_cont(G_F,E^times). A nonzero ideal becomes principal over Be_C; if I Be_C=(f), the associated character is sigma(f)/f. This convention fixes the inverse in the construction back from a twisted invariant section. In particular the general chart need not be principal.
hypotheses: Standing E, F and norm conventions of the reader document; extra restrictions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Independence of the generator follows from Be_C^times=E^times. Locate f in a Banach degree filtration to prove continuity.
Use invariant holomorphic functions and the local-ideal comparison to show an ideal is recovered from its geometric extension, proving injectivity.

For a character choose nonzero sections for both the character and its inverse using positive eigenvector cohomology; their product supplies a nonzero invariant ideal. Verify its geometric extension and character.
acceptance: Both twists are needed to show the invariant ideal is nonzero; continuity of the character is part of the conclusion.

sources.match: Both twists are needed to show the invariant ideal is nonzero; continuity of the character is part of the conclusion.

nodes.title: Generation of P by degree one
nodes.statement: For every perfect F the E-algebra P_F is generated by P_(F,1): Sym^d_E(P_(F,1)) -> P_(F,d) is surjective for every d>=0. Thus each homogeneous section is a finite sum of products of degree-one sections. It need not itself be a single product when F is not algebraically closed.
hypotheses: Standing E, F and norm conventions of the reader document; extra restrictions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Choose two degree-one sections with disjoint orbit divisors, and use their Koszul sequence over the geometric curve.
Twist by a positive power, apply geometric H^1-vanishing, then descend surjectivity using positive-eigenvector Galois cohomology. This handles degrees above the initial quadratic step.

For the quadratic step use a separable totally ramified quadratic coefficient extension, its two-Veronese comparison and faithful scalar descent. In equal characteristic 2 use an Eisenstein polynomial with nonzero derivative, for example X^2+pi X+pi, and the uniformizer unit twist, rather than adjoining a purely inseparable square root.
acceptance: Generation means a sum of products. The source coefficient field is characteristic zero; its equal-characteristic transfer must retain a separable quadratic extension.

sources.match: Generation means a sum of products. The source coefficient field is characteristic zero; its equal-characteristic transfer must retain a separable quadratic extension.

nodes.title: The schematic curve over general F
nodes.statement: The imported X_(F,E)=Proj(P_F) is a regular noetherian integral scheme of dimension one. Its closed points are |Y_F|/phi^Z, the completed local ring at [y] is B_dR,y^plus, and the weight deg([y])=deg(y) gives sum_x deg(x)ord_x(f)=0 for nonzero rational f and H^0(X,O_X)=E. This is completeness in the weighted-curve sense of Definition 5.1.3; no finite-type properness over E is asserted.
hypotheses: Standing E, F and norm conventions of the reader document; extra restrictions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Degree-one generation covers Proj by the Dedekind charts Be_t. Compare their localizations on overlaps through the common invariant meromorphic field.
Identify their maximal ideals and completions with the orbit-point and jet descriptions.

Use the homogeneous quotient degree formula for rational functions to obtain the weighted product formula; a regular global function has no poles and is a constant by the eigenvector unit calculation.
acceptance: The conclusion is a regular noetherian curve, with a specified weighted degree convention, rather than a finite-type E-curve.

sources.match: The conclusion is a regular noetherian curve, with a specified weighted degree convention, rather than a finite-type E-curve.

nodes.title: Rational functions and the ind-scheme quotient
nodes.statement: E(X_F)=Frac(B_F)^{phi=1}. For a nonempty open U, O_X(U) is the intersection of the nonnegative local valuation rings at the closed points of U inside this field. The natural phi-invariant map colim_(compact I subset (0,1)) Spec(B_I) -> X is universal for phi-invariant maps to schemes. Each Spec(B_I)->X is flat; for I=[rho_1,rho_2] with rho_1<=rho_2^q it is faithfully flat. The fpqc equivalence relation is the actual kernel pair over X, not an asserted disjoint union of Frobenius graphs.
hypotheses: Standing E, F and norm conventions of the reader document; extra restrictions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Geometrically write an invariant meromorphic function as a quotient of homogeneous sections of equal degree by clearing its positive and negative orbit divisors.
Over general F, coprime numerator and denominator transform by the same continuous character. Multiply both by a positive section with the inverse character, making them invariant.

Identify opens and regular functions by the Dedekind valuations. On each target affine open use the invariant localization B[1/t]^{phi=1}; glue to prove the universal property. Flatness follows from torsion-free modules over the Dedekind local rings, and the fundamental-annulus condition supplies surjectivity.
acceptance: The quotient is characterized in schemes, with its genuine kernel pair. General-field rational-function descent uses an inverse-character section.

sources.locator: Proposition 6.6.2, pp. 256–257; Proposition 6.7.1 and Remark 6.7.2, pp. 258–259; Proposition 7.4.1, p. 268
sources.match: The quotient is characterized in schemes, with its genuine kernel pair. General-field rational-function descent uses an inverse-character section.

nodes.title: Separable coefficient change of the curve
nodes.statement: Let E-prime/E be finite separable, and assume the residue constants of E-prime embed in F. Then X_(F,E) tensor_E E-prime is canonically X_(F,E-prime), and the projection is finite etale of degree [E-prime:E]. For the unramified part the underlying period ring is unchanged and Frobenius is iterated; for the totally ramified part use the completed tensor comparison and rescale radii by the ramification index. The generic printed identity B_(E-prime)=B_E tensor_E E-prime is not used in the unramified case.
hypotheses: Standing E, F and norm conventions of the reader document; extra restrictions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Split the extension into its unramified and totally ramified parts and use the eigenspace/Veronese comparisons in each case.
Compute the resulting invariant function fields, keeping the Frobenius iteration in the unramified calculation.
At a closed point decompose K_y tensor_E E-prime as a finite product of finite separable fields and compare the corresponding Dedekind localizations. Glue the normal affine charts.

The graded twist over the coefficient field is by tensor powers of a one-dimensional line. A choice of basis gives a graded comparison; changing that basis multiplies degree d by a scalar to the d-th power, hence acts identically on degree-zero basic-open localizations. The resulting Proj map is canonical. Import relativeProj.veroneseIso for every positive Veronese, without a finite-generation assumption.
acceptance: For equal-characteristic inseparable coefficient extensions, the tensor can be nonreduced; they are outside this etale statement.

sources.locator: §6.1.3, p. 244; Theorem 6.5.2(2), pp. 255–256; Proposition 7.5.1, p. 269, with the unramified correction
sources.match: For equal-characteristic inseparable coefficient extensions, the tensor can be nonreduced; they are outside this etale statement.

nodes.title: Finite extensions of the tilt give etale covers
nodes.statement: For finite Galois L/F, X_(L,E)->X_(F,E) is finite etale Galois with group Gal(L/F), of degree [L:F]. Closed-point stabilizers act faithfully as Gal(K_z/K_y) on the corresponding residue fields, so inertia is trivial. Non-Galois finite separable extensions give finite etale maps by passage to a Galois closure.
hypotheses: Standing E, F and norm conventions of the reader document; extra restrictions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Use the finite-orbit point dictionary to identify quotient orbits and the stabilizer action on residue fields.
Radius preservation prevents a Galois element from identifying a point with a nontrivial Frobenius translate.

Choose invariant degree-one sections nonvanishing on a given finite orbit, using positive-eigenvector cohomology, to put each orbit in an invariant Dedekind affine chart. Identify the invariant chart ring with the F-chart. Faithfulness of the stabilizer on residue fields makes the action free on geometric points; apply the existing SF.1 finite-group quotient theorem to obtain the finite etale torsor.
acceptance: Residue stabilizer faithfulness is the no-inertia input; it is stronger than knowing only the quotient set of closed points.

sources.locator: Proposition 7.6.1, pp. 269–270, invoking SGA 1, Exposé V, Corollary 2.4
sources.match: Residue stabilizer faithfulness is the no-inertia input; it is stronger than knowing only the quotient set of closed points.

nodes.title: Curve of the uncompleted algebraic closure
nodes.statement: Define X_(Fbar,E)=lim_(finite L/F in Fbar) X_(L,E) in schemes, with affine chart rings the filtered colimits of the finite-etale Dedekind chart rings. It is a regular noetherian curve with constant field E, despite the infinite tower. There are G_F-equivariant maps X_(C,E)->X_(Fbar,E)->X_(F,E), C=completion(Fbar). Finite-orbit points survive as closed points; a point of X_C with infinite G_F-orbit maps to the generic point of the tower curve.
hypotheses: Standing E, F and norm conventions of the reader document; extra restrictions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Use finite etale affine transition morphisms to construct the scheme inverse limit by its affine chart colimits.

For each finite-orbit point choose a normal finite L/F with G_L contained in all stabilizers of its finitely many geometric conjugates. Its primes are then inert at every later finite stage, with unchanged uniformizer because the chart extensions are etale.

For a nonzero element f from a finite-level chart, the number of primes above its zeros and their orders eventually stabilize. Each local colimit is an unramified DVR with that uniformizer and a growing residue field. Its quotient by the fixed power of the uniformizer is a truncated DVR of fixed length. Thus the colimit quotient is a finite product of such rings; apply the Dedekind quotient criterion. The finite-stage residue fields, and therefore the quotient rings themselves, need not stabilize.
acceptance: The uncompleted algebraic closure and its completion give different curves; the noetherian claim uses eventual inertness, not an arbitrary filtered colimit theorem.

sources.match: The uncompleted algebraic closure and its completion give different curves; the noetherian claim uses eventual inertness, not an arbitrary filtered colimit theorem.

nodes.title: Finite-projective Frobenius modules on B
nodes.statement: Specialize the existing finite-projective semilinear-module pattern of VB1 to the already imported ring B, not to its Robba germ. Objects are finite projective B-modules M with a semilinear Phi whose linearization phi^*M -> M is an isomorphism. Morphisms commute with Phi; tensor products and internal Homs carry the induced Frobenius, and H^0(M)=ker(Phi-1). By HF9 this is also the category of interval bundles on (0,1) with invertible Frobenius descent datum. No equivalence with Frobenius modules over the Robba germ is asserted here.
hypotheses: Standing E, F and norm conventions of the reader document; extra restrictions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Use finite-projective modules over the already imported B; require invertibility of linearized Frobenius in the data.
Use the global-section equivalence for (0,1), and its compatibility with pullback by the radius Frobenius, to compare B-modules with interval bundles carrying Frobenius datum.
Transport tensor, dual and Hom operations through this comparison; verify H^0 is the fixed-vector E-space.

nodes.title: Degree and characters of Frobenius lines
nodes.statement: For a rank-one object (M,Phi), after extension to B_C choose a basis with Phi(e)=lambda e and define deg(M)=-v_pi(lambda). It is independent of basis and additive on tensor products. Degree maps Pic(phi-Mod_B) onto Z, and its kernel Pic^0 is canonically Hom_cont(G_F,E^times) via the action on geometric fixed vectors. The character statement is about degree zero; arbitrary-degree lines do not have a one-dimensional fixed-vector space.
hypotheses: Standing E, F and norm conventions of the reader document; extra restrictions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Use the imported annular Frobenius-descent equivalence and geometric bundle classification to send M tensor B_C to a rank-one bundle O(d) on X_C. Pull back its standard presentation, obtaining a free B_C-module with Frobenius multiplier pi^(-d). A general basis changes this by phi(u)/u, of pi valuation zero by the B-unit description. Half-open interval freeness alone would not provide a basis over B_C.
Solve the geometric degree-zero difference equation to identify its invariant E-line.

Apply effective continuous descent of interval bundles on all compact subintervals to reconstruct the line from its character; use HF9 to recover the B-module. Check inverse constructions and continuity on the same compact norms.

nodes.title: Every positive Frobenius line presents the same curve
nodes.statement: For positive-degree Frobenius lines L_1,L_2, multiplication H^0(L_1) tensor_E H^0(L_2) -> H^0(L_1 tensor L_2) is surjective. For any positive-degree L its section algebra is generated in degree one and X≅Proj(direct_sum_(d>=0) H^0(L^tensor d)), canonically. In particular for lambda in B^times with v_pi(lambda)>0, X≅Proj(direct_sum_(d>=0) B^{phi=lambda^d}).
hypotheses: Standing E, F and norm conventions of the reader document; extra restrictions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Over C write both lines as positive integral twists with continuous characters. Use a two-section Koszul sequence that retains both character twists.
Use positive-eigenvector H^1-vanishing and the separable quadratic/Veronese argument to prove multiplication, including the smallest positive degrees.

For two positive lines replace one by a high tensor power and compare all maps between them on their section-covered affine charts; independence of the map follows from the rank-one interchange identity. Glue inverse scheme maps.

nodes.title: Runge approximation and recovery of the adic curve
nodes.statement: Let I be a compact interval in (0,1) with endpoints in |F^times| and I intersect I^q empty. If t in P_1 has no zeros on Y_I, Be_t is dense in B_I. The ringed scheme (X,O_X), together with all radial Gauss norms, recovers the adic Frobenius quotient. The bare E-scheme without these norms is not asserted to determine that adic space.
hypotheses: Standing E, F and norm conventions of the reader document; extra restrictions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Use the Lubin–Tate period sum L(x)=sum_(n in Z)[x^(q^-n)]pi^n and isolate its dominant Teichmuller term on the whole interval.

Approximate the unit-ball generators [x], [a]/pi and pi/[b]. For the last use pi times (L(epsilon b^(-1/p^n))/L(epsilon))^(p^n), whose dominant term is pi/[b]. Its only denominator is a power of the chosen t=L(epsilon), so it belongs to Be_t. Division by this ratio would instead approximate pi[b] and introduce an inadmissible pole.
Obtain a uniform residue-ball surjection and iterate smaller corrections for density. Complete the chart functions in the specified norms, recover their adic spectra and glue using the radius action.

Import the existing AdicSpaces Layer 6 annular and Frobenius-quotient constructions. In the current Tau Ceti library the Q_p topological carriers spaY/spaX, open quotient map and wandering windows already exist. The target here is their comparison with the completed schematic charts and norms, not a second quotient construction.

sources.match: The compact interval must avoid its Frobenius translate and the chosen pole. Recovery uses the family of norms as additional data.

nodes.title: The period interval site
nodes.statement: Objects are nonempty intervals I in [0,1], with inclusion morphisms. A family (I_alpha) of subintervals is admissible if, for each compact subinterval K of I, there are finitely many compact subintervals K_j of K whose union is K and each K_j is contained in some I_alpha. This finite compact-refinement condition implies union_alpha I_alpha=I. Restriction sends I to B_I. Bundle and coherent-module categories are confined to intervals avoiding 1; the ring site includes both endpoints. Merely requiring finitely many original cover members over K gives an incorrect topology.
hypotheses: Standing E, F and norm conventions of the reader document; extra restrictions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Omit empty intersections. Pull a finite compact refinement back by intersecting with a compact test interval. For composition, refine each compact piece by the finite compact refinements furnished by its member cover. These operations prove the pretopology axioms.
Use the imported faithful restrictions to form the contravariant ring functor.
Separate the topology of the whole interval site from the subsite [0,1) supporting noetherian annular algebra.
acceptance: Finite compact refinements give pullback and composition, admit closed overlapping chains and compact exhaustions, and reject the disjoint adjacent half-open cover. The source finite-original-subcover wording is too weak for the claimed ring sheaf.

sources.match: Finite compact refinements give pullback and composition, admit closed overlapping chains and compact exhaustions, and reject the disjoint adjacent half-open cover. The source finite-original-subcover wording is too weak for the claimed ring sheaf.

nodes.title: Additive endpoint splitting
nodes.statement: For any interval I in [0,1], let I_plus be the convex hull of I union {1} and I_minus the convex hull of I union {0}. Inside B_I, B_I=B_(I_plus)+B_(I_minus). A convergent expansion into Laurent approximants can be split by nonnegative and negative pi-indices: the nonnegative-index pieces sum in B_(I_minus), while the negative-index pieces sum in B_(I_plus). This is a convergent decomposition, not a claim of unique Teichmuller expansions for every completed element.

nodes.title: Mayer–Vietoris and acyclicity on intervals
nodes.statement: For intervals I,J in [0,1] with nonempty intersection, 0 -> B_(I union J) -> B_I direct_sum B_J -> B_(I intersect J) -> 0 is exact, with last map (f,g) |-> f-g. nodes.title: Period functions as a Frechet–Stein algebra
nodes.statement: For I subset [0,1), choose an increasing compact exhaustion J_n. The Banach rings B_(J_n) are noetherian, their restriction maps are flat and have dense image, and B_I=lim_n B_(J_n) is a Frechet–Stein E-algebra in the imported ND.2 sense. Its coherent systems and coadmissible modules therefore have exact global sections and B_J tensor_(B_I) Gamma(M)=M_J. Generic Frechet–Stein algebras, coadmissibility and their Theorems A/B are imported, not defined again here.
hypotheses: Standing E, F and norm conventions of the reader document; extra restrictions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Use the compact field/PID dichotomy for noetherianity. A restriction is an injective map into a domain and hence torsion-free over the source PID, giving flatness.
Density follows from the common Laurent subring. Use endpoint maximum norms and a cofinal exhaustion for the defining seminorms.
Apply the imported coadmissible theorems, and compare an arbitrary compact J with a sufficiently large exhaustion member.

nodes.title: Bundles and coherent systems on intervals
nodes.statement: For I subset [0,1), define Fib(Y_I) as the 2-limit over compact nonempty J subset I of finite projective B_J-modules, and Coh(Y_I) as the corresponding 2-limit of finitely generated B_J-modules. Each object includes isomorphisms M_J tensor_(B_J) B_K ≅ M_K for K subset J, satisfying the identity and triple-inclusion cocycle conditions; morphisms commute with these isomorphisms. The categories of modules at a fixed ring use the existing generic finite-projective and coherent-module infrastructure.

proofSteps: Form compatible systems in the imported module categories; the compact PID/field theorem makes each bundle system finite free at a compact stage.
Define restriction by retaining the smaller compact intervals and identify cofinal compact exhaustions.
Use the interval sheaf property and the gluing theorem to identify these systems with locally free, respectively coherent, O-modules on the subsite.

nodes.title: Global sections of interval bundles
nodes.statement: For I subset [0,1), Gamma: Fib(Y_I) -> finite-projective B_I-modules is an exact tensor equivalence, with inverse M |-> (M tensor_(B_I) B_J)_J. It commutes with restriction to compact intervals. For I=(0,rho], all these modules are finite free. The generic affine-scheme finite-projective/vector-bundle equivalence is existing work in current TauCetiRoadmap AlgebraicVectorBundles; the target here is the noncompact interval comparison.

proofSteps: Apply the imported Frechet–Stein exactness and base-change theorem to the compatible compact bundle system.

Supply G-GENERATORS: produce one finite family of compatible global sections generating on every compact annulus, with bounded approximation estimates. This gives a surjection O^n->E of coherent systems and a kernel bundle K.

Because E_J is finite free on every compact J, Hom(E_J,O_J^n)->Hom(E_J,E_J) is surjective. Apply exact global sections to these coherent Hom systems and lift id_E to a global splitting E->O^n. The resulting finite B_I-module is a direct summand of B_I^n, hence finite projective. This avoids any false assertion that classical compact points cover every maximal ideal of B_I.

Use base change and exactness to prove the mutually inverse tensor functors. For I=(0,rho], finite projectives over the Bezout domain are free. The splitting also gives a finitely generated kernel; it is not an independent consequence of bounded coadmissible rank.

nodes.title: Coherent systems and bounded fibres
nodes.statement: For I subset [0,1), Gamma identifies Coh(Y_I) with the coadmissible B_I-modules. Such a module is noncanonically M direct_sum product_(y in Y_I) N_y, where M is finite projective, N_y is a finitely generated torsion B_dR,y^plus-module, and the nonzero N_y have locally finite support on compact annuli. It is finitely presented over B_I iff the dimensions of all fibres over k(y) are uniformly bounded. The lengths of the torsion modules themselves need not be bounded.

proofSteps: Use the imported coadmissible equivalence for the first assertion. At each compact PID split off its finite torsion submodule, identify the torsion through the local DVR jets, and pass to the locally finite product.
Lift the projective quotient using exact global sections and the bundle equivalence; choose a splitting to obtain the noncanonical direct sum.

Finite presentation bounds all fibre dimensions. Conversely a uniform bound supplies uniformly bounded compact presentations; use the generator approximation obligation and coherent exactness to obtain a global finite presentation.

nodes.title: Finite etale extension of compact period annuli
nodes.statement: Let L/F be finite (hence separable, since F is perfect), and let I be a compact interval in [0,1) with nonzero endpoints in |F^times|. Then B_(L,I) is finite etale of constant degree [L:F] over B_(F,I); for a Galois extension its automorphism group is Gal(L/F). For the spectral unit balls, [epsilon] B_(F,I)^circ is contained in Tr_(L/F)(B_(L,I)^circ) for every nonzero epsilon in m_F. At I={0} this is the unramified Witt-field extension. Moreover the spectral unit-ball extension is almost finite etale for the ideal generated by [m_F] in the coefficient integral ring. Its almost finite projectivity and almost vanishing cotangent complex are proved through the same root-refined discriminant estimates; this is stronger than the displayed trace inclusion.
hypotheses: Standing E, F and norm conventions of the reader document; extra restrictions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Choose an integral primitive element alpha and b with b O_L subset O_F[alpha]. Replace alpha by alpha^(1/p^k) so |b^(1/p^k)| exceeds the outer radius.

Lift the basis through Witt digits and contract the residual error on the compact annulus. This yields generation over B_(F,I), with rational coefficients, not generation of the whole ring over its unit ball.
Compare Galois conjugates for independence and degree. The discriminants of the root-refined bases approach norm 1 uniformly on I; the trace dual basis gives etaleness and the almost trace estimate.

Use discriminant-dual finite subalgebras with annihilator losses tending to the almost ideal to obtain almost finite projectivity and almost vanishing of differentials; compare with parent almost purity on the annular adic pair. Do not replace almost etaleness by trace-surjectivity alone.

The equivalence and fixed-vector inverse commute with interval restriction, tensor products and Frobenius. The compact descent theorem for value-group endpoints must be extended to arbitrary compact subintervals by G-RADIUS before taking the limit; density of |F^times| alone does not cover an irrational singleton or an included irrational endpoint.

For B_(0,1]=B^plus[1/[varpi]], finite F-extension need not produce the asserted finite-etale annular algebra. Likewise Frobenius modules over B^plus fail the Galois descent satisfied over B. The positivity boundary quotient retains residue-field Frobenius information that global B-descent loses.

Identifying such a representation and checking the comparison is the concrete counterexample obligation G-BOUNDARY.

nodes.statement: For E=Q_p and F=C_p^flat, choose a convex decreasing sequence beta_j in Z[1/p] tending to an irrational beta>0. With Y=[p^flat], put f=sum_(i>=0) p^i Y^(beta_(2i)) and g=sum_(i>=0) p^i Y^(beta_(2i+1)). The two-generated ideal (f,g) is not principal in A[1/p], and remains nonprincipal in B^plus. nodes.title: A strict endomorphism of a completed algebraic closure
nodes.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p and C_k a completed algebraic closure of k((t)). There is a continuous k-linear field endomorphism C_k->C_k which is not surjective. One may first adjoin algebraic residue constants inside C_k to run the explicit construction, so it does not require the given k itself to contain infinitely many algebraic constants.

Let x represent the resulting primitive extension of k((t)). The completed differential estimate kills d(t) relative to the constant field. After interchanging x and t, the extension over k((x)) is topologically algebraic by the primitive differential criterion.

Thus the completed algebraic closure of k((t)) embeds strictly into one of k((x)); identify the latter abstractly and topologically with the former to get the strict endomorphism. The analytic differential and type-IV inputs are the exact R-KT supplier request.

gaps.title: A quantitative proof of interval matrix gluing
gaps.detail: The corrected local factorization theorem has a neighborhood depending on the chosen matrix Z. The source then chooses Z to approximate U without bounding that dependence. Prove a uniform bound or a different bounded-ring approximation giving exact-square module surjectivity for every gluing datum. RF4 requires this surjectivity and maximum-spectrum coverage; ring Mayer–Vietoris alone supplies neither module effectivity nor the missing bound.

gaps.title: Uniform generation for interval bundles
gaps.detail: Supply the analytic bounded-generator argument for compatible compact finite-free systems of bounded rank, producing one finite family of global sections generating every compact restriction. Generic Frechet–Stein coadmissibility does not imply finite generation. After this step, exactness on coherent Hom systems splits the finite-free presentation and proves projectivity, without claiming compact classical points exhaust the maximal spectrum. Prove the half-open freeness and closed-submodule conclusions with the same explicit compatible approximations.

gaps.title: Concrete boundary-one counterexample
gaps.detail: Write out a finite F-extension for which the endpoint-one annular claim fails, and separately a continuous G_F-representation not factoring through G_(k_F) whose associated B-Frobenius module is outside the B-plus essential image of Remark 11.1.11. Check the relevant comparison rather than using failure of a contraction estimate as a counterexample.

gaps.title: Valued homogeneity in the maximally complete Cp-type case
gaps.detail: Prove the automorphism extension theorem for a maximally complete algebraically closed field with the Cp-type residue field and value group, allowing positive valuation rescaling. The conditional orbit formula is established as a target; maximal completeness for an arbitrary value group is insufficient to infer the transitivity hypothesis. No available-source proof of this extension theorem has been read.

gaps.detail: Verify the equal-characteristic Lubin–Tate supplier extension R-LT and the quantitative descent arguments R-TATE in that setting. The displayed Q_p formula is established as a target; the source q-only auxiliary polygon does not justify applying it literally to arbitrary E.

gaps.detail: Extend the value-group-endpoint compact descent theorem to every compact J subset [0,1), including an irrational singleton and an included irrational endpoint.
